article.headline: Yaté and Thio face orange weather alert as heavy rains hit territory
article.summary: Météo-France has placed Yaté and Thio under orange alert for heavy rain and storms until Friday afternoon.
article.body:
Up to 150 mm of rain may fall locally in just twelve hours between Thursday night and Friday in Yaté and Thio, according to Météo-France. While these two communes face an orange alert, the rest of New Caledonia remains under a yellow weather watch. In these yellow-alert areas, meteorologists forecast accumulation totals of 50 to 100 mm over a twelve-hour period.

Following heavy rainfall, authorities urge the public to limit travel to essential needs only. Residents are advised not to cross flooded roads or bridges, even on foot, and to keep children away from streams and rivers. The municipality of Ouégoa warned that rising waters could potentially submerge the Mission bridge at Bondé, noting that the radier at the Paimboa tribe has already been inundated.

According to NoumeaPost, a slow meteorological improvement is expected starting Friday, particularly in the South, where showers are becoming less frequent. However, the Northeast remains exposed to stormy downpours capable of generating significant local accumulation. Winds are generally blowing from the East between 15 and 20 knots, with the possibility of gusts during thunderstorms.

Looking ahead to the weekend, conditions will remain very cloudy across the country. Saturday will bring frequent and locally sustained showers, especially on the East Coast, the mountain range, Belep, the Isle of Pines, Lifou, and Maré. By Sunday, although the weather will stay cloudy, precipitation is expected to become more infrequent. Temperatures are forecast to rise, climbing above seasonal averages by the end of the weekend as the wind shifts and eases across the region.

news.title: 43 WTC wickets, still benched: Mohammed Siraj overlooked again as India hand Gurnoor Brar debut cap in 2nd Test against New Zealand
news.og_title: 43 WTC wickets, still benched: Mohammed Siraj overlooked again as India hand Gurnoor Brar debut cap in 2nd Test against New Zealand
news.og_desc: Despite questions surrounding his omission from the opening Test and growing calls for his inclusion, Mohammed Siraj has once again been left out of India's playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand. The decision comes despite Siraj being India's highest wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, with 43 wickets in 11 matches. Siraj's continued absence comes after India's bowling attack struggled to bowl out New Zealand in the series opener, with the visitors managing to hold their ground and secure a draw. His omission has therefore attracted attention, particularly given his impressive record and consistent contributions in the longest format. Since his memorable performance in last year's Oval Test, where he bowled India to an incredible six-run victory over England, Siraj has taken 21 wickets in seven Tests played in Asian conditions at an impressive average of 21.28, including a four-wicket haul. For the series opener, India opted for Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as their four specialist pacers, with Washington Sundar providing an additional bowling option. The team management's selection was understood to be based on the bowling combination and the need for extra batting depth. However, despite the bowling unit's inability to dismiss New Zealand in the first Test, Siraj has failed to find a place in the playing XI once again. His omission leaves India without their leading wicket-taker in the ongoing WTC cycle as they look to strengthen their position in the series. Meanwhile, Ravindra Jadeja has also been left out of the playing XI, while young pacer Gurnoor Brar has been handed his maiden Test cap, becoming the 321st player to represent India in the longest format. Brar's inclusion marks a significant opportunity for the debutant as India look for a more effective bowling performance in the second Test. With the series finely poised after the opening Test ended in a draw, India's decision to persist with the bowling combination while leaving out Siraj will remain one of the key talking points. (ANI)

news.og_title: سياسي / وزارة الخارجية: المملكة تدين وتستنكر بأشدّ العبارات العدوان الإيراني الآثم على دولة الكويت
news.og_desc:
الرياض 16 جمادى الآخرة 1448 هـ الموافق 26 نوفمبر 2026 م واس
    أعربت وزارة الخارجية عن إدانة واستنكار المملكة العربية السعودية بأشدّ العبارات العدوان الإيراني الآثم على دولة الكويت الشقيقة، باستهداف أحد المواقع الحيوية، وتسبب بوفاة وإصابة عدد من الأشخاص.
    وقالت الوزارة في بيان: "إن الاعتداءات الإيرانية المتواصلة تعني مزيدًا من التوتر وزعزعة الاستقرار، والمملكة تجدّد تأكيدها على أن هذه الانتهاكات تقوض الجهود الدولية الهادفة لاستعادة الأمن والاستقرار في المنطقة".
    وأضافت: " المملكة تحمل إيران عواقب استمرارها في هذه الاعتداءات الغاشمة، وتطالبها بالوقف الفوري لهذه الانتهاكات، وتجدّد تضامنها الكامل مع دولة الكويت الشقيقة في ما تتخذه من إجراءات للحفاظ على سيادتها".
    // انتهى //
